package_info.why_malicious: The package is a trojanized clone of a legitimate library, containing hidden code that extracts and executes a command-and-control (C2) payload from an embedded image file during installation, enabling remote code execution and exfiltration of command results.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code spawns a detached Node.js process to execute the malicious loadformat.js script, ensuring the payload runs independently of the main process.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Spawning a detached process to run an additional script during installation is highly unusual for a legitimate package.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not execute hidden scripts or spawn detached processes during installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may run postinstall scripts for setup, but not to execute hidden or unrelated code.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At installation, the code reads embedded image files, extracts ASCII payloads, and if a threshold is met, dynamically executes the extracted code as JavaScript, enabling arbitrary code execution from image-embedded payloads.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Extracting and executing code from image files is a classic steganography-based evasion technique, not used in legitimate packages.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not extract and execute code from image files during installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use of image processing would not involve dynamic code execution.
key_indicators: Dynamic code execution from image data

execution_context.file_location: payload extracted from logo2.jpg, executed in memory

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After installation, the code registers the infected host with a remote C2 server, periodically fetches and executes attacker-supplied commands, and exfiltrates command output to the C2 server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Establishing a persistent C2 channel, executing arbitrary commands, and exfiltrating results are hallmarks of remote access trojans.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not establish C2 channels or execute arbitrary remote commands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; this is classic C2 malware behavior.

attack_chain.action: During installation, index.js spawns a detached process to execute loadformat.js.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of the malicious loader script.

attack_chain.action: loadformat.js reads image files, extracts ASCII payloads, and dynamically executes code if a threshold is met.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of the C2 payload if present in image.

attack_chain.action: Extracted C2 payload registers the client, polls for commands, executes them, and exfiltrates results.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full remote control and data exfiltration.

behavioral_signatures: Postinstall script spawns detached Node.js processes
Image files read and parsed for ASCII payloads
Dynamic code execution from image-extracted strings
Outbound HTTPS connections to hardcoded IPs for registration and polling
Periodic polling for remote commands and execution
file_indicators: logo1.jpg, logo2.jpg, logo3.jpg in package root
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages that spawn detached processes during installation, read and parse image files for ASCII payloads, or dynamically execute code extracted from non-code files. Flag packages making outbound connections to suspicious or hardcoded IPs (e.g., 85.208.108.29) or exhibiting periodic polling for remote commands. Look for the presence of suspicious image files and loader scripts in package contents.
